reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 shows a mixed, non-uniform oxide scale (Mn, Cr, Fe oxides) on a similar alloy, not a continuous Cr2O3-rich layer. E2 discusses a different processing method (microwave cladding) and a different alloy (Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20), not the effect of increasing Cr in FeNiCrCoCu. E3 describes a dense but unstable, local oxide layer on a different HEA (AlCrFeNiV) and attributes wear resistance to fine microstructure and hard phases, not a continuous Cr2O3 barrier.
premises: Increasing Cr content in FeNiCrCoCu promotes a continuous Cr2O3-rich oxide layer during high-temperature sliding.
A continuous Cr2O3-rich oxide layer reduces subsurface plastic deformation during wear.
A continuous Cr2O3-rich oxide layer improves overall wear resistance.
The oxide layer acts as a barrier to dislocation motion and grain boundary movement.
